    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}

    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in

    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[
    43	    \lambda_z(c)^2=
    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
   219	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]
   220	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   221	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   222	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   223	  \begin{align}
   224	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   225	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   226	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   227	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   228	  \end{align}
   229	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   230	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   232	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   233	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   234	  \end{equation}
   235	  The ratio supremum $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over all real unit $H^1$ profiles equals
   236	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.
   237	\end{proposition}
   238	
   239	\begin{proof}
   240	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   241	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   242	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   243	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   244	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   245	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   246	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   247	  convention gives
   248	  \[
   249	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   250	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   251	  \]
   252	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   253	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   254	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   255	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   256	  \[
   257	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   258	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   259	  \]
   260	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   261	
   262	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   263	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   264	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   265	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   266	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   267	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   268	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   269	
   270	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   271	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   272	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   273	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   274	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   275	  continuity.
   276	
   277	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   278	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   279	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   280	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   281	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   282	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   283	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   284	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   285	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   286	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   287	
   288	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   289	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   290	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   291	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   292	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   293	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   294	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   295	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   296	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   297	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   298	\end{proof}

   300	\begin{proposition}[The spatial energy and static lower variational expression]
   301	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}
   302	  Over all real unit $H^1$ profiles define the energy
   303	  \[
   304	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   305	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}
   306	    \left(A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)-\frac{b(g)}2\right).
   307	  \]
   308	  Then
   309	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-energy-map}
   310	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   311	    =\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   312	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{2/(2-\alpha)}
   313	    \in(0,\infty).
   314	  \end{equation}
   315	  In particular,
   316	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   317	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}),
   318	    \qquad
   319	    F_0(z)=k\left[
   320	    \frac{(2z/(2-\alpha))^{(2-\alpha)/2}}{8q^{q/2}}
   321	    \right]^{1/k},\quad z>0.
   322	  \end{equation}
   323	  The subscript in $F_0$ labels this scalar map; the covariance retains its
   324	  original temporal exponent $a$.
   325	\end{proposition}

   350	\subsection{The kernel row and full occupation energy}
   351	
   352	Define, for $u \ne 0$,
   353	\begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-damped-kernel}
   354	  K_\star(u)=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}
   355	  \int_0^\infty
   356	  e^{-(\lambda+\lambda^2/(2D))|u|}
   357	  \lambda^{a-1}\ud\lambda,
   358	\end{equation}
   359	and set $K_\star(0) = 0$ for time integration.
   360	
   361	\begin{lemma}[Exact row maximum]\label{L:occupation-kernel-row}
   362	  The kernel is even, positive off zero, locally integrable, decreasing on
   363	  $(0,\infty)$, and $K_\star(u) \le |u|^{-a}$ off zero. Its exact row maximum on
   364	  $[0,1]$ is
   365	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-kernel-row}
   366	    \max_{s\in[0,1]}\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud t
   367	    =R_\star:=2\int_0^{1/2}K_\star(u)\ud u\in(0,\infty).
   368	  \end{equation}
   369	\end{lemma}
   370	
   371	\begin{proof}
   372	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   373	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   374	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =
   375	  \int_0^tK_\star(u)\ud u$. It is concave because its integrand is decreasing on
   376	  positive arguments. The row is $\Phi(s)+\Phi(1-s) \le 2\Phi(1/2)$, with
   377	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   378	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
   379	\end{proof}
   380	
   381	Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the full class of strongly $H^1(\R^d;\R)$-measurable fields
   382	$s\mapsto g_s$ on $(0,1)$ with $\|g_s\|_2 = 1$ a.e. and $T(g) =
   383	\int_0^1b(g_s)\ud s < \infty$. No time smoothness, common compact support or
   384	optimizer condition is imposed.
   385	
   386	\begin{proposition}[The full physical occupation class]
   387	  \label{P:occupation-physical-class}
   388	  The pairings $(s,t)\mapsto B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)$ are measurable,
   389	  representative independent and equal to their physical integrals. With
   390	  \[
   391	    J(g)=\int_0^1\int_0^1
   392	    K_\star(s-t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,
   393	  \]
   394	  every $g \in \mathcal{O}$ satisfies
   395	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-physical-bound}
   396	    0\le J(g)\le R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty.
   397	  \end{equation}
   398	  The energy over exactly this full class satisfies
   399	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-own-energy}
   400	    0<\mathcal{E}_\star^{\mathcal{O}}
   401	    :=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\big(J(g)-T(g)/2\big)
   402	    \le R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty.
   403	  \end{equation}
   404	\end{proposition}
   405	
   406	\begin{proof}
   407	  The map $s\mapsto b(g_s)$ is measurable by continuity of the squared gradient
   408	  norm. Also $\int_0^1\|g_s\|_{H^1}^2\ud s = 1+T(g)$. Use a separably valued
   409	  strong representative and replace exceptional null times by one fixed real
   410	  unit compact bump. Joint measurable spatial representatives exist: approximate
   411	  this Bochner $L^2$ field by simple $H^1$-valued functions with summable
   412	  $L^2(0,1;H^1)$ errors, and choose measurable spatial versions for their
   413	  countably many values. A subsequence has a measurable spacetime $L^2$ limit,
   414	  and for a.e. $s$ its spatial $L^2$ class is $g_s$.
   415	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair} makes every pairing independent of the
   416	  spatial versions. The continuous pairing map on the separable space $H^1\times
   417	  H^1$ from Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} consequently gives a
   418	  measurable function of $(s,t)$ agreeing a.e. with the nonnegative physical
   419	  integral.
   420	
   421	  Set $F(s) = b(g_s)^{\alpha/4}$. Equations~\eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}
   422	  and~\eqref{E:spatial-square-CS} give $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   423	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}F(s)F(t)$. Since $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$, concavity on the unit time
   424	  interval yields $\int_0^1F^2 = \int_0^1b(g_s)^{\alpha/2}\ud s \le
   425	  T(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Now use $2F(s)F(t) \le F(s)^2+F(t)^2$ and the exact row
   426	  bound \eqref{E:occupation-kernel-row}, whose column bound is the same because
   427	  $K_\star$ is even, to obtain \eqref{E:occupation-physical-bound}. Positive
   428	  Tonelli is valid before finiteness is known. Null-time modifications affect
   429	  only a product-null set, so they cannot change $J$.
   430	
   431	  The scalar maximum of $R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T^{\alpha/2}-T/2$ over $T \ge 0$
   432	  is $R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}$, by the same
   433	  differentiation as~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. This bounds the occupation
   434	  supremum from above. For positivity take a constant-in-time unit compact
   435	  profile and its spatial dilation $U_\ell$. Its $J$ is $J_0\ell^\alpha
   436	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)$, where $J_0 = \int_0^1\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud s\ud t \in
   437	  (0,\infty)$, while $T = \ell^2b(g)$. For sufficiently small $\ell > 0$,
   438	  $\alpha < 2$ makes $J-T/2 > 0$. Thus, the nonempty supremum is a positive
   439	  finite real number. This is a comparison bound; no attaining profile or
   440	  equality in it has been asserted. No spatial point trace or rough stochastic
   441	  evolution was used. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:occupation-physical-class}.
   442	\end{proof}

   447	zero, with the profile constant in time for the latter. No zero-gradient unit
   448	state is used. The temporal identities remain valid, and the moment model is the

    12	inequality recorded by Sz.-Nagy~\cite{sz.nagy:source1941:integralungleichungen}*{(2),
   101	\begin{theorem}[Explicit white moment bounds]\label{T:white-moment-bounds}
   102	  For the same original point limit,
   103	  \begin{equation}\label{E:white-moment-bounds}
   104	    \frac23\sqrt{\frac{c}{M_a}}\le C_2(c,a)
   105	    \le\frac23\sqrt{cK_0(a)},\qquad
   106	    K_0(a)=\frac{2^a}{1-a},\quad
   107	    M_a=\frac{\Gamma_E((1+a)/2)}
   108	    {\Gamma_E(1+a)\Gamma_E((1-a)/2)} .
   109	  \end{equation}
   110	  Its time exponent is $(3-a)/2$. These are bounds, not a numerical evaluation
   111	  of the intrinsic supremum.

   114	\begin{proof}
   115	  Here $q = 3,k = 2,m = 3/2$. Formula~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   116	  gives
   117	  \[
   118	    F_0(z)=2\left[\frac{(2z)^{1/2}}{8\,3^{3/2}}\right]^{1/2}.
   119	  \]
   120	  For $c > 0$, $\sqrt{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}} = c/\sqrt3$, hence
   121	  $F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}) = \sqrt c/(3\sqrt2)$ and
   122	  $2^mF_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}) = (2/3)\sqrt c$. Substitution into
   123	  Corollary~\ref{C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}
   124	  proves~\eqref{E:white-moment-bounds} in the original units. All Gamma factors
   125	  are positive finite for $0 < a < 1$. At $c = 0$, $u = 1$ and $C_2 = 0$ by
   126	  Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment}; both displayed bounds vanish. This
   127	  proves Theorem~\ref{T:white-moment-bounds}.

   130	\begin{corollary}[Uniform relative width of the bound formulas]
   131	  \label{C:white-relative-width}
   132	  For $c > 0$, the ratio of the upper and lower formulas is
   133	  \[
   134	    \sqrt{K_0(a)M_a}
   135	    \le\left[\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2\Gamma_E(5/4)^2}\right]^{1/2},
   136	  \]
